```{r}
#B1

students <- data.frame(
  id         = 1:8,
  name       = c("Alice", "Bruno", "Chen", "Dana", "Elif", "Farid", "Grace", "Hiro"),
  sex        = c("F", "M", "M", "F", "F", "M", "F", "M"),
  section    = c("A", "B", "A", "C", "B", "C", "A", "B"),
  midterm    = c(78, 85, 92, 67, 74, 88, 95, 59),
  final      = c(82, 79, 96, 71, 80, 91, 93, 65),
  attendance = c(95, 88, 100, 72, 90, 85, 98, 60),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

```

```{r}
#B2

str(students)
dim(students)     # 8 7
names(students)   # "id" "name" "sex" "section" "midterm" "final" "attendance"
summary(students)

```

```{r}
#B3

students$average <- round((students$midterm + students$final) / 2, 1)
students$average
# 80.0 82.0 94.0 69.0 77.0 89.5 94.0 62.0

```

```{r}
#B4

students$passed <- students$average >= 70 & students$attendance >= 75
students$passed
# TRUE TRUE TRUE FALSE TRUE TRUE TRUE FALSE

```

```{r}
#B5

students$standing <- ifelse(students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                     ifelse(students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))
students[, c("name", "average", "standing")]

```

```{r}
#B6

classify <- function(score) {
  if (score >= 85) {
    "Distinction"
  } else if (score >= 70) {
    "Merit"
  } else if (score >= 50) {
    "Pass"
  } else {
    "Fail"
  }
}

result <- sapply(c(90, 73, 55, 40), classify)
print(result)
# [1] "Distinction" "Merit"       "Pass"        "Fail"

```

```{r}
#C1

new_students <- data.frame(
  id         = c(9, 10),
  name       = c("Ines", "Jamal"),
  sex        = c("F", "M"),
  section    = c("C", "A"),
  midterm    = c(81, 70),
  final      = c(84, 68),
  attendance = c(92, 80),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)

new_students$average  <- round((new_students$midterm + new_students$final) / 2, 1)
new_students$passed   <- new_students$average >= 70 & new_students$attendance >= 75
new_students$standing <- ifelse(new_students$average >= 90, "Honors",
                         ifelse(new_students$average >= 75, "Good", "Needs Support"))

students_all <- rbind(students, new_students)
students_all[9:10, c("name", "average", "passed", "standing")]

```

```{r}
#C2

quiz <- c(8, 7, 10, 6, 7, 9, 10, 5, 8, 6)
students_all <- cbind(students_all, quiz = quiz)
class(students_all)   # "data.frame"

```

```{r}
#C3

m <- cbind(midterm = students_all$midterm, final = students_all$final)
m <- rbind(m, mean = colMeans(m))
m

```

```{r}
#C4

# rbind() stacks data frames on top of each other, but the column names have to
# match. If they don't, R gives an error: "names do not match previous names".
# The assignment says 2-3 sentences, so I used tryCatch() to catch the error
# so the code doesn't crash and just prints a message instead.

bad <- new_students
names(bad)[2] <- "student_name"   # changed "name" to "student_name" so it doesn't match students

tryCatch(rbind(students, bad),
         error = function(e) {
           message("rbind failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
           NULL
         })

# Output:
# rbind failed: names do not match previous names
# NULL

```

```{r}
#E1

students_all$section <- factor(students_all$section)
students_all$sex     <- factor(students_all$sex)

levels(students_all$sex)       # "F" "M"
levels(students_all$section)   # "A" "B" "C"

```

```{r}
#E2

table(students_all$sex)
# F M
# 5 5

table(students_all$section)
# A B C
# 4 3 3

table(students_all$sex, students_all$section)

```

```{r}
#E3

as.integer(students_all$sex)
# 1 2 2 1 1 2 1 2 1 2

# The integers are the codes R uses to store the factor. R doesn't keep "F" and "M"
# as text, it saves them as numbers and keeps a list of levels to match them to.
# Level 1 is "F" and level 2 is "M" (alphabetical order), so 1 = F and 2 = M.
# For example, Alice is F so she gets 1 and Bruno is M so he gets 2.

```

```{r}
#E4

students_all$sex_label <- factor(students_all$sex,
                                 levels = c("F", "M"),
                                 labels = c("Female", "Male"))
levels(students_all$sex_label)   # "Female" "Male"

```

```{r}
#E5

summary(students_all$sex_label)
# Female   Male
#      5      5

mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Female"])   # 80.5
mean(students_all$average[students_all$sex_label == "Male"])     # 79.3

```
